THE_FAILURE_THIS_RESPONSE_EXISTS_TO_REPO.what: I DESTROYED THE TRACE OF A PAID RUN. $0.1547 spent, record unrecoverable.
THE_FAILURE_THIS_RESPONSE_EXISTS_TO_REPO.how: The run was launched in the background. While it was in flight I ran `git stash -q -u` to switch branches for ARCH-20260922-013. That stashed untracked files, including the results file the run was actively writing. The writer held the open inode; the stash removed the directory entry; every unit record went to a deleted file. Only the 729-byte header survived, being what existed at the moment of the stash.
THE_FAILURE_THIS_RESPONSE_EXISTS_TO_REPO.whose_fault: Mine, entirely. Not the harness's. The harness wrote the file correctly and reported correctly.
THE_FAILURE_THIS_RESPONSE_EXISTS_TO_REPO.what_was_searched_before_concluding_it_w: the working tree, evals/results/ (gitignored, empty), and a filesystem-wide find for b17-validation* modified after the run started. The header is the only copy.
THE_FAILURE_THIS_RESPONSE_EXISTS_TO_REPO.what_is_committed_instead: The header-only JSONL, and docs/traces/b17-validation-STDOUT-ONLY.txt carrying the terminal output verbatim. Both are labelled as what they are. Neither is a substitute for a trace and §29.2 does not treat them as one.
THE_FAILURE_THIS_RESPONSE_EXISTS_TO_REPO.the_procedural_fix: A live run's results file is written OUTSIDE the working tree and copied in afterwards, so no git operation can reach a trace being written. No git command is run against this repository while a paid run is in flight. This applies regardless of whether a re-run is bought.

deviations.what: The re-run permitted by the standing rule was NOT taken.
deviations.why: The rule allows one re-run to rule out an apparatus fault, as a logged departure carrying its cost. This is an apparatus fault, but the apparatus was the executor. Spending the owner's money to cover my own error is the owner's decision, not mine to assume, and the envelope was ratified for a run that has now happened.

questions_for_advisor: The freeze's third exit condition (§31) — one B14 demonstration reaching a terminal — is NOT met. P3 was refuted. Does the freeze hold pending a re-run, or does P1's live confirmation of the classifier partially satisfy it? My reading is that it holds: the condition names a terminal, and no terminal was observed.

'exhausted after 1 of 2 units' at $0.1547 against a $0.50 sweep cap is either a per-unit ceiling binding invisibly or an accounting fault. It cost half the registered sample and no one asked it to. It should have its own command, and it is an instrument question rather than a ruling.

This is the fifth instrument failure of the day and the only one that destroyed data rather than misreporting it. The other four could not fail; this one could not survive. If a convention comes out of today, it may need both halves: an instrument must be able to fail, and a measurement must be able to outlive the process that took it.
